name: Chinese Classical Mahjong
description: Chinese Classical Mahjong is a traditional four-player Mahjong ruleset emphasizing classic hand structure, open information management, and fan-based scoring categories grounded in older Chinese table practice.

overview.description: Chinese Classical Mahjong is a traditional four-player Mahjong ruleset emphasizing classic hand structure, open information management, and fan-based scoring categories grounded in older Chinese table practice.

history.origins: Chinese Classical Mahjong preserves rule ideas from early widespread Chinese Mahjong forms before heavy modern regional standardization.
timeline: 19th century: Core Mahjong mechanics formed in late Qing-era Chinese play.
Early 20th century: Classical forms circulated through treaty ports and social clubs.
Modern era: Classical reconstructions retained in rules literature and enthusiast groups.
history.cultural: Represents the historic core from which many later regional Mahjong systems evolved.
history.evolution: Regional branches diverged from classical foundations, but the classical form remains a useful baseline for comparative Mahjong rules analysis.

setup.deck: Standard Mahjong set including suited tiles, winds, dragons, and optional flowers/seasons.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 tiles; East starts with 14 and discards first.

rules.objective: Complete a legal winning hand with four melds and one pair while meeting table scoring requirements.
rules.gameplay: Play proceeds by drawing from the wall and discarding. Players may claim discards for Chow, Pung, or Kong subject to priority and seat restrictions. A player wins by self-draw or discard claim when hand structure and scoring conditions are satisfied.
keyRules: Turn flow is draw then discard, with claim interruptions handled by priority.
Chow claims are position-limited; Pung and Kong claims have broader access.
Winning hand is based on four melds plus one pair with table-specific scoring thresholds.

strategy.basic: Build efficient waits and avoid committing to rigid high-variance hand shapes too early.
strategy.intermediate: Use discard reading and visible tile tracking to balance speed against safety.
strategy.advanced: Adjust hand value ambitions dynamically based on opponent pressure and tile-flow information.
tips: Prefer two-sided waits over closed middle waits when speed matters.
Retain flexible tiles early until your scoring route is stable.

variations.name: Flower/Season Use
variations.description: Tables differ on how flower and season bonuses are counted and replaced.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is scoring-policy level, not structural engine change.

synthesis.shortDescription: Chinese Classical Mahjong is a traditional four-player Mahjong variant focused on classical meld structure and fan-based scoring.
